states.gap: Tighter leading: line pitch 74.0px against A's 76.0px, and B's type is ~1.5% larger (advance 26.4px vs 25.8px), so normalised the leading is ~1.68 vs A's ~1.77 — roughly 4-5% less air between lines, a slightly denser grey over a full screen. B also gives the page no floor: text runs to a hard clip at y=1800 with the next line sliced through its x-height, versus A's 35px of clearance before its rule.
states.gapTheirs: Three different left edges on one page: body prose starts at x=623px, but the H1's text starts at x=673 and the H2's at x=697 because the '#'/'##' sit inline instead of hanging — the prose spine jogs right by 50px and 74px (25 and 37 CSS px) at every heading, where B holds a single flush edge at x=624 with markers hung out at x=546-596. Compounding it, A spends 123px of the 1800px viewport (6.8%) on furniture: a 63px title bar carrying 'Untitled.md' plus two icons, and a hairline at y=1748 under a '188 words / 961 characters / 1 min read' strip.
states.verdict: Same paper (#F9F9F9 corner to corner in both), same measure (623-2241px, ~62 characters), same paragraph rhythm (exactly 2x line pitch) — so the whole argument is what surrounds the text, and A loses it. A's headings shove their words 25 and 37 CSS px off the paragraph edge, which means the one thing a writer stares at all day, the left spine, wobbles every time the piece changes gear; B hangs the markers into the margin and the edge never moves. Then A charges you 63px at the top for a filename you already know and 60px at the bottom for a word count that will pull your eye down on every line you finish. B's leading is the tighter of the two by about 4%, and that is the only thing I would take back from it.

states.name: narrow
states.gap: Zero bottom gutter: the second list line is guillotined mid-glyph at the 1800px viewport edge (ink runs to y=1753 and the next line's ascenders are sliced), whereas A leaves 35px of paper below its last line. Also tighter leading — 74px pitch vs A's 76px on a ~43.5px em, i.e. ~1.67 vs ~1.75.
states.gapTheirs: 108px of permanent furniture on the page: a 60px title bar (sidebar toggle, 'Untitled.md', format menu) plus a 172px bottom band with a #DFDFDF hairline and a live '188 words / 961 characters / 1 min read' counter — B shows 1920x1800 of nothing but paper and text. Compounding it, A's '#' sits inline at the body edge (x=143), so heading text starts at x=200 against body text at x=144: the left margin breaks by 56px (2 characters) at every heading, while B hangs '#' and '-' 54px into the gutter and holds one unbroken left rule at x=183.
states.verdict: B is the page; A is an app with a page inside it. A gives you 2px more air per line and a quieter #9E9E9E for its markers, then spends that goodwill on a title bar you never read and a word counter parked permanently under your last sentence — the exact thing a novelist covers with a sticky note. B's hanging markers buy the one thing A can't fake: a single true left edge at x=183 that headings, body and bullets all obey, at a 58-character measure instead of A's 62. B still deserves the criticism that it forgot the bottom margin entirely — writing near the end of the document means typing with the window edge shaving your descenders — but one missing gutter is a smaller sin than two bands of chrome and a left margin that jumps two characters every time you write a heading.
